title: Align capital gains tax rates with income tax rates
registry_rule: The reform specification and the ELASTICITY SWEEP for the Budget's flagship measure. Two legs are computed per elasticity: the reform against the certified baseline, and the baseline itself. The published comparison is post-behavioural against OBR's post-behavioural costing when it lands; the static leg is published beside it as the wedge, because that wedge IS the disagreement.
behavioural_finding:
VERIFIED against the certified engine, and it changes what this lane is. gov.simulation.capital_gains_responses.elasticity is ZERO from 2000-01-01, and capital_gains_behavioural_response short-circuits to 0 when the elasticity is 0. So a default PolicyEngine-UK score of this measure is STATIC — the engine does not hand you a behavioural number, it hands you the machinery to compute one once YOU supply an elasticity. The response also requires simulation.baseline to be attached, so it only exists in a reform run.

That means the elasticity is an ASSUMPTION THIS REPO MAKES, not a property of the engine, and it is the single parameter the whole comparison turns on. Published estimates of this measure disagree mostly about the realisations response; reported receipts have ranged widely on a broadly stable rate structure. So the lane does not pick one value and publish a number — it sweeps, and every sweep point must carry a citation before anything is published from it.

elasticity_sweep.label: static
elasticity_sweep.source: The certified engine's own default (policyengine_uk/parameters/gov/simulation/capital_gains_responses/elasticity.yaml, 2000-01-01: 0). Publishing this leg needs no external citation because it asserts no behaviour.

elasticity_sweep.label: central
elasticity_sweep.note: A central realisations elasticity must be taken from a named published source — an HMRC or OBR costing note, or an academic estimate for the UK — with the definition it uses (semi-elasticity vs elasticity, and with respect to WHICH rate). Until that citation exists this sweep point is not runnable and the validator refuses to mark it publishable.

elasticity_sweep.label: high_response
elasticity_sweep.note: The upper end of the published range, so the lane reports an interval rather than a point. Same citation rule.

comparison_rule: Compare LIKE FOR LIKE. OBR costings of this measure will be post-behavioural; the static leg is not comparable to them and must never be presented as though it were — that is the #67 finding one level up. The static-vs-behavioural difference is published as its own quantity on the behavioural_elasticity axis, not folded into a residual.
not_yet_run: This spec is unexecuted. The compute needs the managed environment and the certified populace-uk bundle, exactly like #51 and #66; a local Microsimulation() refuses without an explicit dataset. Everything below the engine boundary — the reform values, the paths, the baselines, the sweep contract — is verified and tested here.
